question: How do full-batch gradient descent, SGD, and mini-batch SGD differ in how they estimate the gradient?
direct_answer: Full-batch GD uses the whole dataset, SGD uses one example at a time, and mini-batch SGD uses a small subset of examples.
expanded_answer: The difference is the source of the gradient estimate. Full-batch gradient descent computes the exact gradient of the empirical loss over all training samples, so its updates are stable but expensive. Stochastic gradient descent replaces that with a single sample, making each update noisy but cheap. Mini-batch SGD is the middle ground: it averages gradients over a small batch, trading off computational efficiency, noise, and stability.
key_points: SGD: noisy but very cheap updates
Noise can help exploration but also adds variance
common_wrong_ideas: SGD and mini-batch GD are the same thing
Full-batch GD is always better because it is more accurate
Noise in SGD is purely a bug
